put.1956.0.B5.reviewed_statement: Consider a set of $ 2 n $ points in space, $ n>1 $. Suppose they are joined by at least $ n^{2}+1 $ segments. Show that at least one triangle is formed. Show that for each $ n $ it is possible to have $ 2 n $ points joined by $ n^{2} $ segments without any triangles being formed.

put.1956.0.B7.text: Incomplete source condition: unequal constant polynomials can satisfy both empty-root-set conditions. The standard nonconstant-polynomial interpretation is required; it is not explicitly stated in either available transcription.
put.1956.0.B7.reviewed_statement:
The polynomials $ P(z) $ and $ Q(z) $ with complex coefficients have the same set of numbers for their zeros but possibly different multiplicities. The same is true of the polynomials
$$
P(z)+1 \text { and } Q(z)+1
$$

Prove that $ P(z) \equiv Q(z) $.

put.1957.0.A3.text: Editorial correction: k>1 is required for the strict inequality. The longer transcription says positive integer, which would include k=1 and give 0<0. The secondary source explicitly excludes that case.
put.1957.0.A3.reviewed_statement:
$ A $ and $ B $ are real numbers and $ k $ an integer greater than 1. Show that
$$
\left|\frac{\cos k B \cos A-\cos k A \cos B}{\cos B-\cos A}\right|<k^{2}-1
$$
whenever the left side is defined.

put.1958.1.A3.text: Source convention: successive random choices are independent and uniform on [0,1].
put.1958.1.A3.reviewed_statement: Real numbers are chosen at random from the interval $ (0 \leq x \leq 1) $. If after choosing the $ n $th number the sum of the numbers so chosen first exceeds 1 , show that the expected or average value for $ n $ is $ e $.

put.1958.1.A6.text: Source convention: a positive annual interest rate is assumed for a finite perpetuity investment.
put.1958.1.A6.reviewed_statement: What is the smallest amount that may be invested at interest rate $ i $, compounded annually, in order that one may withdraw 1 dollar at the end of the first year, 4 dollars at the end of the second year, $ \ldots, n^{2} $ dollars at the end of the $ n $th year, in perpetuity?

put.1958.1.B4.text: Source convention: the two points are independently uniform with respect to surface area.
put.1958.1.B4.reviewed_statement: What is the average straight line distance between two points on a sphere of radius $ 1 ? $

put.1958.2.B5.text: Source convention: successive turns have the same directed angle. The phrase if there is one retains the possible absence of a finite limiting point.
put.1958.2.B5.reviewed_statement: The lengths of successive segments of a broken line are represented by the successive terms of the harmonic progression $ 1,1 / 2,1 / 3, \ldots, 1 / n, \ldots $. Each segment makes with the preceding segment a given angle $ \theta $. What is the distance and what is the direction of the limiting point (if there is one) from the initial point of the first segment?

put.1959.0.B5.text: Unresolved source variant: the sign of the constant in the first line differs between the two available transcriptions (+4 versus -4). This published record retains +4 and is not certified against an original examination.
put.1959.0.B5.reviewed_statement: Find the equation of the smallest sphere which is tangent to both of the lines: (i) $ x=t+1, y=2 t+4, z=-3 t+5 $, and (ii) $ x=4 t-12, y= $ $ -t+8, z=t+17 $.

put.1960.0.A6.text: Source convention: throws of the six-sided die are independent and each face has probability 1/6, as made explicit by the secondary version.
put.1960.0.A6.reviewed_statement: A player throwing a die scores as many points as on the top face of the die and is to play until his score reaches or passes a total $ n $. Denote by $ p(n) $ the probability of making exactly the total $ n $, and find the value of $ \lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} p(n) $.

put.1961.0.B2.text: Source convention: both points are chosen independently and uniformly along the segment.
put.1961.0.B2.reviewed_statement: Let $ \alpha $ and $ \beta $ be given positive real numbers, with $ \alpha<\beta $. If two points are selected at random from a straight line segment of length $ \beta $, what is the probability that the distance between them is at least $ \alpha $ ?

put.1962.0.A2.text: Source convention: the geometric mean is the nonnegative square root and the stated averages must exist. No squared-equation variant is substituted.
put.1962.0.A2.reviewed_statement: Find every real-valued function $ f $ whose domain is an interval $ I $ (finite or infinite) having 0 as a left-hand endpoint, such that for every positive member $ x $ of $ I $ the average of $ f $ over the closed interval $ [0, x] $ is equal to the geometric mean of the numbers $ f(0) $ and $ f(x) $.

put.1962.0.B3.text: Source convention: region means an open region. Scholes makes openness explicit; the boundedness assertion fails for arbitrary non-open convex sets.
put.1962.0.B3.reviewed_statement: Let $ S $ be a convex region in the Euclidean plane containing the origin. Assume that every ray (that is, half-line) from the origin has at least one point outside $ S $. Prove that $ S $ is bounded. (A region in the plane is defined to be convex if and only if the line segment joining every pair of its points lies entirely within the region.)

put.1962.0.B6.text: Editorial correction: exactly 2n equality points are required, as specified by Scholes, to exclude constant functions. This is an edited formulation, not a claim about the exact printed examination wording.
put.1962.0.B6.reviewed_statement: Let $f(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}(a_k\sin kx+b_k\cos kx)$, where $n$ is a positive integer and $a_k,b_k$ are real constants. Suppose $|f(x)|\leq1$ for $0\leq x\leq2\pi$, and $|f(x)|=1$ at exactly $2n$ distinct points in $[0,2\pi)$. Show that $f(x)=\cos(nx+a)$ for some real constant $a$.

put.1964.0.B1.text: Editorial correction: the sequence consists of positive integers, as specified by the secondary source.
put.1964.0.B1.reviewed_statement:
Let $ u_{k}(k=1,2, \ldots) $ be a sequence of positive integers, and let $ V_{n} $ be the number of those which are less than or equal to $ n $. Show that if
$$
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 1 / u_{k}<\infty
$$
then
$$
\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} V_{n} / n=0
$$
